subject: Rollout scoping workshop with operations
body: Two hours with Dale and four DC managers. Agreed the rollout order — Memphis, Reno, then the Ohio cluster. Dale wants a single go-live weekend per site rather than a phased cutover.

subject: Security review cleared
body: Eugene signed off the architecture review. The only condition is SSO through their existing identity provider from day one, which is already in the statement of work.

subject: Call with Dale on the MSA redlines
body: Legal is holding on the liability cap and the 30-day termination clause. Dale will push for a decision at Thursday's commercial review. Confident, but would not commit to a date.

subject: Re: FY27 budget freeze
body: Dale confirmed the freeze lifts on 1 September and that the rollout is line item 14 in the approved capital plan. He asked whether we can start onboarding before the paperwork lands.

subject: Intro call with Marisol on yard visibility
body: Marisol has no live view of which trailers are on which dock. She estimates two hours a day of shunting that would not happen with a yard map. No budget of her own.

subject: Site walk at the Memphis DC
body: Offered the 19th or the 26th. Marisol prefers the 26th so the new dock scheduling shift pattern has bedded in. Asked her to include the yard supervisor.

subject: Driver app raised in passing
body: Dale mentioned that the driver app contract renews in March and that he is not happy with it. Nothing more than a signal at this point — logged so it does not get lost.

subject: Discovery session with clinical informatics
body: Renata walked us through the current scheduling process across three of the acute sites. Consultant rota changes are handled by email and re-keyed by hand, which is where the errors come from.

subject: Introduction to Curtis Nwachukwu
body: Thirty minutes, mostly Curtis asking about implementation risk rather than price. He wants a named clinical sponsor on any project over $250k, which Renata will need to become or find.

subject: Proposal and three-year pricing sent
body: Sent the proposal with a phased option — two acute sites in year one, the rest in year two. Renata confirmed receipt and said she would circulate it before governance.

subject: Security questionnaire outstanding
body: Their questionnaire is 214 questions and IT governance will not table the proposal without it. Ours is 80% pre-answered from the library; the gaps are all about their specific EHR integration.

subject: Bed-flow requirements call
body: Wesley wants to predict discharge readiness 24 hours ahead. He has been keeping his own spreadsheet since January and it is better than anything the trust provides him.

subject: Sample data request for the bed-flow model
body: Asked for six months of anonymised admissions and discharge timestamps. Wesley has forwarded it to their privacy office, who quote four weeks for a data-sharing agreement.

subject: Outpatient expansion flagged by Renata
body: Renata raised the outpatient clinics unprompted at the end of our call. She thinks 18 of the 60 are in the FY27 plan but wants to check before we write anything down.

subject: Partner-led introduction with Ewan
body: Our delivery partner brought us in on the back of their network modelling work. Ewan already had a budget line and a regulatory deadline, which is why this has moved as fast as it has.

subject: Deal desk approved the 4% uplift cap
body: Internal. Deal desk approved capping the annual uplift at 4% for the three-year term in exchange for annual prepayment. No further concessions authorised without a new approval.

subject: Supplier re-registration started
body: Arjun opened the re-registration on the procurement portal on 3 August. Ten working days, so 17 August at the earliest. Nothing we can do to accelerate it.

subject: Commercial terms review
body: Agreed everything: three-year term, 4% uplift cap, annual prepayment, and a 90-day exit for convenience after year two. Ewan said he would sign once procurement clears the registration.

subject: Chasing the signed order form
body: Short note to Ewan confirming the order form matches what we agreed on the 6th and asking him to sign as soon as the portal clears. No response yet.

subject: Outage communications demo
body: Demoed the proactive notification flow to Bethan and two of her team leads. The question that stuck was whether we can suppress notifications for planned works, which we can.

subject: Add-on proposal sent to Bethan
body: Priced as an add-on to the grid programme rather than standalone, which saves them roughly 30%. Flagged that the pricing holds only if both are signed in the same order.

subject: Inbound enquiry from the metering programme
body: Website enquiry naming the smart metering programme. Ewan confirmed it is a different director's budget and offered to make an introduction, which is the fastest route in.

subject: Referral call from Orrery Robotics
body: Matthias at Orrery introduced us to Lieke. First call was mostly Lieke testing whether we understood arable agronomy, which the pilot data answered better than we could have.

subject: Pilot results review
body: Pieter's team modelled 11,000 hectares and beat their in-house baseline by six points on yield prediction error. Lieke asked for the methodology write-up to share with her board.

subject: Contract signed
body: Two-year term signed. Lieke agreed to act as a reference for other agritech prospects and to co-present at the growers' conference in November.

subject: Onboarding kickoff scheduled
body: Account-level note. Onboarding starts 14 July with Pieter's team. Not tied to a deal — this is delivery, but worth having on the account timeline.

subject: Sensor expansion scoping
body: Pieter wants 300 additional sensors across the eastern trial sites. His constraint is the autumn drilling window — anything that arrives after early October is useless until spring.

subject: Indicative pricing for 300 additional sensors
body: Sent indicative pricing to Lieke with a caveat on lead time. She replied within the hour saying the number is fine and to sort out the dates with Pieter.

subject: Referred by an operating partner
body: One of Hugh's operating partners saw the portfolio pack at another firm and asked who built it. Imogen picked up the thread from there.

subject: Reporting requirements workshop
body: Imogen spends roughly four days a quarter assembling the pack by hand across 22 portfolio companies. Half of that is chasing companies for numbers, which we cannot fix; the other half we can.

subject: Proposal sent with two commercial options
body: Two options: annual rolling, or three years with a discount and a fixed uplift. Hugh will want the discount and to keep the annual break, so expect a negotiation on term length.

subject: Inbound question about diligence workspaces
body: Imogen asked, almost as an afterthought at the end of an unrelated email, whether we do anything for live diligence. Answered briefly and offered a call in September.

subject: Trial feedback call with Omar
body: Omar had the forecast API in production against two client accounts within a fortnight. His only complaint was rate limiting on backfill, which we raised as a product request.

subject: Order form countersigned
body: Twelve-month licence countersigned. Shauna asked to be invoiced quarterly, which finance approved.

subject: Benchmark dataset scoping
body: Shauna wants regional benchmarks she can put in front of her own clients. That is a redistribution question rather than a pricing one, and it needs a legal answer before anything else.

subject: Sample benchmark extract sent
body: Sent Omar a two-region sample so he can judge the granularity. He came back the same day asking for store-format splits, which we do not currently publish.

subject: Fleet scheduling discovery
body: Annika runs 14 vessels against a whiteboard and a shared calendar. She was clear about the problem and equally clear that she cannot approve anything on this scale herself.

subject: Request for time with Jesper
body: Asked Annika to introduce us to Jesper. She agreed in principle but has not made it happen — she is deep in the summer charter season.

subject: Deal has not moved since June
body: Fifty-four days in discovery with no decision date. Two options: escalate to Jesper directly and risk irritating Annika, or accept that this lands in next year's budget. Escalating.

subject: Inbound call about inspection reporting
body: Freya rang after seeing the scheduling demo materials circulating internally. Her inspection reports go to clients, so the formatting and audit trail matter more than the analysis.

subject: Platform migration discovery
body: Fionnuala walked us through the subscriber estate. Their incumbent platform is 11 years old and nobody defends it, but the migration cost is the whole argument.

subject: Migration proposal sent
body: Proposal included a phased migration by title to keep the cash cost inside one financial year. Fionnuala said it was the right shape but that the timing was wrong.

subject: Fionnuala confirmed no decision this year
body: The board will not fund a platform migration in the same year as the print restructure. She was straight with us about it, which is worth something. Revisit after February results.

subject: Desmond asked about events CRM
body: Desmond emailed directly after hearing about the subscriber conversation. His events business is profitable and he implied he has discretion over his own tooling budget.

subject: Met Matthias at the automation expo
body: Twenty minutes at the stand. Matthias described unplanned stops on the electronics lines as his single biggest measured problem, and asked for a trial before he would talk numbers.

subject: Trial on the Eindhoven line
body: Two-week trial on one cell. Unplanned stops fell by roughly a third. Matthias has the figures and is prepared to stand behind them internally.

subject: Proposal sent to Saskia and Matthias
body: Priced for four cells with an option on the remaining six. Copied Saskia directly for the first time — she has not engaged with us at all so far.

subject: Follow-up on the proposal
body: Matthias says Saskia has read it and has questions but has not written them down. Asked him to get them in writing before the 20 August operations review.

subject: Spares forecasting requirements
body: Tobias is carrying €1.4m of slow-moving spares and is measured on it quarterly. He wants a forecast he can defend to finance, not a dashboard.

subject: Still waiting on the parts history
body: Two years of parts movement has been promised twice and not delivered. The bottleneck is their ERP team, not Tobias. Nothing here progresses until the extract lands.

subject: Executive briefing with supplier quality
body: Gwen brought eight people. Their supplier corrective-action cycle averages 47 days and their customers have started asking about it, which is the pressure behind this programme.

subject: Export-control review passed
body: Their trade compliance team cleared the architecture on 29 July, subject to no technical data leaving the country of origin. That condition is what makes the Ontario residency question load-bearing.

subject: Data residency for the Ontario plant
body: Gwen needs a written commitment that Ontario data stays in Canada. A verbal assurance from us is not enough for her compliance team. Escalated to infrastructure the same afternoon.

subject: Re: five-year agreement structure
body: Roland wants the five-year term broken into an initial three with two optional years at pre-agreed pricing. Workable, but it changes the year-one recognition and needs deal desk.

subject: MRO analytics scoping workshop
body: Yasmin wants the pilot narrow enough to run without a steering committee. Settled on one fleet type and two maintenance bases as the scope.

subject: Pilot proposal sent to Yasmin
body: Six-month pilot priced separately from the supplier quality programme, deliberately, so neither holds up the other. Yasmin confirmed she has the discretionary budget for a pilot at this size.

subject: Introductory call with Devon
body: Gwen passed Devon our details. They lose around 90 tools a year across three plants and currently track them on laminated cards. No budget identified.

subject: Cold-chain pilot review
body: Lucia ran the pilot on eight trailers for three weeks. Two temperature excursions caught in transit that would previously have been found at the depot.

subject: Signed for three sites
body: Brandt signed for three sites on 29 May. April's spoilage incident cost them more than the contract does, so the business case never needed defending.

subject: Line walkthrough at Ridgefield
body: Walked three lines with Lucia. She has timed 14 changeovers by hand and the spread is 22 to 71 minutes for the same product pair. That variance is the entire pitch.

subject: Draft business case for OEE tracking
body: Sent Brandt a one-page case built on Lucia's changeover figures. He replied asking whether the cold-chain contract can be amended rather than adding a second agreement.

subject: Introduction to Hollis in quality assurance
body: Account-level introduction, no deal attached. Hollis owns their audit evidence and would be a stakeholder in anything we do at the plants, so worth knowing early.

subject: Met Nerys at the retail operations forum
body: Nerys sought us out after the panel. Her 240 stores each run their own compliance checklist and she has no way to see completion centrally.

subject: Quarterly check-in with Nerys
body: Relationship call rather than a deal call. Useful context: Simeon has told the operations function he will not read two business cases from them this year.

subject: Store operations discovery
body: Half a day with Nerys and two regional managers. The compliance checklist is the visible problem; the real one is that nobody trusts the completion figures they already have.

subject: Simeon wants a single business case
body: Confirmed with Nerys: store operations and returns must arrive as one paper or neither gets read. Restructuring the proposal accordingly rather than arguing the point.

subject: Returns analytics enquiry
body: Tallulah enquired through the website. Returns run at 18% on garden furniture and she has no analysis of why.

subject: Closed as no decision — sponsor left
body: The sponsor left in May and nobody picked this up. Tallulah still wants it but cannot fund it. Folding the requirement into the store operations case rather than keeping it open.

subject: Partner introduction to Jarrah
body: Our regional partner made the introduction. Quandong would embed our forecasting inside their planner rather than resell it, so this eventually becomes a rev-share conversation.

subject: Integration questions from Inés
body: Inés asked five specific questions about rate limits, webhook retries, and backfill. Answered four; the retry semantics need a product answer.

subject: Milk quality traceability intro
body: Margot knows exactly where the traceability gaps are — collection to intake is a paper record. She also has no budget and no route to one on her own.

subject: Request for a meeting with Hemi
body: Asked Margot to introduce us to Hemi before the October member vote. Capital decisions go to the members, so the timeline is fixed regardless of what we do.
